summary: Computes layover compensation from arrived/available timestamps, free-time thresholds, day-count rules, and contract caps, returning payable layover units and amount.
Computes driver-assist charges from pieces, weight, time, or flat-fee rules, applying customer-specific minimums, maximums, and per-stop conditions.
Computes reimbursable lumper amount from receipts, approval limits, markups, and pass-through policies, returning carrier pay and customer bill values.
Computes escort or pilot-car charges from route segments, jurisdiction requirements, trip counts, and contracted pass-through or marked-up billing rules.
Computes oversize or overweight permit charges from state-level permit schedules, number of jurisdictions, and billing markup policies.
Computes tarp accessorials from tarp count, tarp type, commodity requirements, and customer or carrier compensation schedules.
Computes securement charges from strap count, chain count, commodity minimum-securement rules, and contractual per-unit fees.
Computes team-service premium based on miles, urgency tier, service-level commitments, and contract-specific multipliers or flat additions.
Computes inside-delivery accessorials from service level, floor count, elevator availability, piece count, and minimum charge rules.
Computes residential delivery charges using destination type, shipment mode, parcel/LTL thresholds, and customer contract tariffs.
Computes limited-access surcharges from destination category mappings, stop type, and tariff rules including one-time-per-stop application.
Computes sort-and-segregate charges from SKU count, pallet count, line-item complexity, labor-time rules, and per-stop minimums.
Computes freeze-protection accessorials from temperature thresholds, lane seasonality, equipment type, and contractual daily or trip pricing.
Computes after-hours service charges from appointment time, local business-hour calendars, day-of-week rules, and contractual premiums.
Computes weekend service surcharges based on pickup or delivery day, service commitment, and lane- or customer-specific fee schedules.
Computes redelivery charges from failed-attempt reasons, customer fault rules, distance retraced, and tariff minimums.
Computes reconsignment charges from instruction timing, miles already traveled, stop changes, and tariff or contractual flat-fee rules.
Computes diversion charges from in-transit reroute timing, route delta miles, extra stops, and diversion tariff logic.
Computes pallet exchange debits or credits from pallet type, pallets tendered and returned, tolerance rules, and reimbursement schedules.
Computes net freight weight from gross weight, pallet count, pallet tare schedules, and commodity-specific allowance caps.
Computes trailer washout reimbursement from commodity contamination class, required wash level, receipt limits, and contract pass-through policies.
Computes truck-order-not-used charges from cancellation timing, dispatch status milestones, deadhead incurred, and contract-specific TONU formulas distinct from general tonu rules.
Evaluates whether liability, cargo, and other insurance coverages satisfy customer and load requirements, returning compliance flags and deficiency reasons.
Computes whether a carrier’s operating authority age meets onboarding or load-specific minimum-age rules with optional waiver thresholds.
Evaluates carrier eligibility against safety score thresholds, intervention status, and configurable exception rules, returning pass/fail and violated criteria.
Checks whether required equipment certifications such as food-grade, liftgate, or air-ride meet load requirements using effective dates and type matches.
Computes next trailer inspection due date or overdue status from prior inspection dates, mileage intervals, and jurisdictional maintenance rules.
Computes CDL medical card expiration status, grace-period handling, and next due threshold for dispatch eligibility.
Computes required random-test selection counts from active driver population, period rates, and regulatory rounding rules.
Evaluates whether dimensions and weight exceed legal limits by jurisdiction and determines which permit or escort requirement flags apply.
Computes whether a load requires trailer seals based on commodity, customer, border crossing, and security-program rules.
Evaluates whether planned setpoint ranges and transit duration satisfy product temperature requirements and tolerance bands.
Computes whether chains are required on a route from elevation, season, weather flags, and state chain-law rules.
Evaluates whether a driver’s endorsements such as hazmat, tanker, or doubles satisfy load and equipment requirements.
Computes whether a tractor and trailer pairing is valid based on fifth-wheel, axle, ABS, reefer power, and connection compatibility rules.
Computes estimated axle-group loading from cargo placement, trailer geometry, and tandem positions, returning legal and target balance values.
Computes trailer cube used, remaining capacity, and utilization percentage from shipment dimensions, stackability rules, and equipment interior dimensions.
Computes pallet fit counts and layout feasibility from pallet footprints, trailer dimensions, turn allowances, and no-stack constraints.
Computes total route miles from an ordered stop sequence, stop coordinates or mile legs, and optional out-of-route penalties.
Computes non-revenue miles from tractor start position, repositioning legs, and loaded-route segmentation rules.
Computes payable deadhead compensation from approved empty miles, free-mile thresholds, pay rate type, and contract caps.
Computes linehaul pay from loaded miles under practical, shortest, or paid-mile rules with customer or carrier mileage overrides.
Computes a route sequence score from backtracking, service windows, handling complexity, and detention risk factors for dispatch comparison.
Evaluates whether a proposed pickup and delivery appointment set is feasible given transit time, dwell assumptions, and HOS-derived available hours.
Computes expected stop dwell from facility historical benchmarks, appointment type, commodity, and load/unload method rules.
Computes relay handoff mile splits, timing, and pay apportionment between drivers based on route legs and service constraints.
Computes repositioning distance from delivery to next likely freight origin or terminal under configurable bounce-planning rules.
Computes a risk score for missing service commitments using remaining miles, available hours, weather penalty inputs, and stop complexity factors.
Evaluates whether a load can be executed as drop-and-hook from trailer availability, yard inventory assumptions, and customer equipment rules.
Computes expected yard move duration from facility size, spot distance, congestion factor, and trailer readiness assumptions.
Computes trailer spotting charges from move count, standby time, hostler type, and contractual minimum billing increments.
Computes trailer pool surplus or deficit by location from starting inventory, inbound and outbound events, and target pool levels.
Computes storage charges for trailers or containers from dwell duration, free days, day-rate tiers, and customer-specific caps.
Computes utilization percentages for trailer fleets from loaded days, idle days, maintenance downtime, and available-equipment counts.
Evaluates whether a pickup number format and checksum satisfy customer-specific validation rules, returning validity and normalized form.
Computes normalized bill-of-lading reference components from raw strings using token rules, prefix mappings, and duplicate suppression.
Computes grouped purchase-order totals, distinct counts, and billing splits from shipment line associations and customer consolidation rules.
Allocates charges, weight, and revenue across split shipments using proportional, equal, or line-based allocation rules.
Computes consolidated billing totals and child-shipment rollups under master bill rules including duplicate-charge suppression.
Computes a standardized stop sequence and roles from EDI 204 stop segments using stop-type precedence and de-duplication rules.
Maps raw EDI 214 event codes into canonical tracking statuses using code tables, exception precedence, and milestone business rules.
Computes normalized invoice charge categories from EDI 210 line items using accessorial code maps, precedence rules, and fallback defaults.
Computes functional acknowledgment outcome from accepted and rejected transaction counts with control-number balancing rules.
Computes the next EDI control number given current value, min/max bounds, and rollover policies.
Computes expected segment counts for transaction validation from segment lists while applying ST/SE inclusion rules.
Computes canonical business-party roles from EDI N1 qualifiers using transaction-type-specific precedence rules.
Computes preferred shipment references from multiple EDI L11 identifiers using qualifier ranking and customer-specific selection rules.
Converts EDI-provided units of measure into canonical internal units with transaction-specific overrides and rounding rules.
Computes canonical milestone dates from EDI date/time qualifiers using event precedence and timezone-offset assumptions.
Computes linehaul amount from paid miles and contracted per-mile rates with breakpoints, minimums, and rounding rules.
Computes charges from billed weight under CWT tariffs, weight breaks, deficit rating logic, and minimum charges.
Computes linehaul from piece count using per-piece tariffs, break thresholds, and stop- or shipment-level minimums.
Computes minimum customer sell rate required to satisfy margin targets after carrier cost, fuel, and expected accessorial assumptions.
Computes gross spread and margin percentage between customer charge and carrier cost with inclusion rules for fuel and accessorial components.
Computes sell price from carrier or modeled cost plus markup percentages or fixed margin adders under configurable inclusion rules.
Computes the customer rate needed to achieve a target gross margin percentage from projected cost and surcharge composition.
Computes equivalent rating factors when converting between truckload, LTL, drayage, or flatbed pricing bases using configured formulas.
Computes NMFC-style density class from weight and cubic dimensions using density brackets and dimensional rounding rules.
Computes dimensional billed weight from shipment dimensions, divisor tables, and mode-specific rounding rules.
Computes whether rating at the next weight break yields a lower total charge and returns the applicable deficit-rated amount.
Computes charges from mileage bands, lane tiers, and breakpoint logic with optional directional or region-specific modifiers.
Computes apportioned registration cost allocation by jurisdiction from fleet miles and registration schedules for internal settlement purposes.
Computes road-use tax liability from taxable miles, jurisdiction rates, and exempt-mile rules.
Allocates toll costs to loads, drivers, or customers based on route segments, loaded versus empty legs, and split-allocation rules.
Computes owner-operator linehaul settlement from gross linehaul revenue, pay percentage or rate basis, authorized deductions, and settlement caps.
Computes owner-operator fuel surcharge share from billed FSC, contract split percentages, and inclusion or exclusion of empty-mile components.
Computes payable accessorial amounts to owner-operators from billed accessorials, pass-through rules, and item-specific pay percentages.
Computes escrow deductions and remaining balances for owner-operators based on weekly withholding rules, balance caps, and release schedules.
Computes maintenance-fund deductions from mileage, percentage-of-revenue, or flat periodic rules with cap enforcement.
Computes settlement deductions for prior cash advances using repayment percentages, minimum net-pay protections, and outstanding balances.
Computes factoring-fee deductions from eligible receivable amounts, fee rates, reserve percentages, and exclusion rules.
Computes trailer rental charges owed by an owner-operator from rental periods, weekly proration rules, and utilization-based waivers.
Computes settlement insurance deductions from enrolled coverage types, policy period proration, and contribution schedules.
Allocates cargo claims, service penalties, or other chargebacks to settlements using fault percentages, cap rules, and multi-load attribution logic.
Computes final owner-operator net settlement by combining gross pay, reimbursements, deductions, reserves, and minimum-net-pay rules.
Computes non-taxable per diem amounts from nights away, dispatch-day rules, and owner-operator or driver eligibility limits.
Computes driver payroll from payable miles, pay rates, split-team logic, and guaranteed minimum compensation rules.
Computes payroll from worked hours, overtime thresholds, premium categories, and rounding increments.
Computes stop pay from compensated pickup and delivery counts, excluded stop types, and team or trainer split rules.
Computes driver detention payroll from unpaid free time, approved detention windows, and pay-rate tiers independent of customer billing rules.
Computes driver layover payroll from qualifying layover events, 24-hour qualification rules, and flat or tiered pay schedules.
Computes driver breakdown compensation from repair downtime, waiting thresholds, and daily or hourly pay caps.
Evaluates payroll bonus eligibility from service, safety, utilization, and attendance metrics against configurable threshold rules.
Computes bonus amounts from eligible performance metrics, tier tables, and payout caps or floors.
Computes payroll allocation between trainer and trainee based on miles, trip phases, and training-program split percentages.
Computes which settlement period a load belongs to from delivery, paperwork-received, or approval dates using cutoff calendars.
Allocates a payment across open invoices using customer remittance preferences, oldest-first or exact-match rules, and residual balancing.
Computes invoice due dates from issue date, terms days, end-of-month conventions, and holiday or weekend rolling rules.
Computes customer early-payment discounts from invoice amount, discount terms, eligibility windows, and excluded charge categories.
Computes late-payment charges from overdue days, grace periods, statutory or contractual rate methods, and compounding rules.
Computes net payable after offsetting reciprocal receivables and payables subject to legal-entity and aging eligibility rules.
Computes releasable reserve amounts from aging thresholds, claim holds, and minimum-balance retention rules.
Computes underpayment variance between expected and received invoice amounts, allocating differences by disputed charge categories.
Computes the next invoice state from approval, send, payment, dispute, and void flags using deterministic status precedence rules.
Evaluates whether a customer should be on credit hold based on aging balances, credit limit usage, dispute exceptions, and grace rules.
Computes expected credit-loss reserve from receivable aging buckets, customer risk classes, and recovery-rate assumptions.
Computes estimated cargo-claim liability from declared value, shipment weight, released-value limits, salvage offsets, and deductible rules.
Computes the final valid cargo-claim filing date from delivery date, concealed-damage rules, and contract or statutory limitation periods.
Computes whether a concealed-damage notice was timely given delivery date, notice timestamp, and customer-specific business-day rules.
Computes net claim exposure after salvage percentage, recovery value, disposal costs, and insurer participation rules.
Allocates a claim amount across line items, packages, or involved carriers based on value, weight, fault, or contractual contribution rules.
Computes overage-shortage-damage variance by comparing tendered, loaded, delivered, and exception quantities under tolerance rules.
Computes contractual penalties for missed appointments or service failures from breach type, grace periods, and cap rules.
Computes expected fuel consumption uplift from temperature, wind, precipitation, terrain factors, and equipment type assumptions.
Computes fuel consumed during idling from idle hours, engine burn rates, APUs, and reefer interaction rules.
Computes reefer fuel usage from setpoint, ambient conditions, mode, run hours, and trailer-specific burn-rate tables.
Computes optimal fuel stop intervals from tank capacity, usable reserve, route miles, mpg assumptions, and stop-count minimization rules.
Allocates fuel purchases across trips or jurisdictions using odometer spans, trip dates, and proportional-mile or actual-consumption rules.
Computes tractor operating cost per mile from fixed costs, variable costs, utilization assumptions, and maintenance reserves.
Computes trailer ownership or lease cost per day from depreciation, financing, fixed expenses, and available days.
Computes next maintenance due thresholds from current miles, engine hours, prior service points, and service schedule rules.
Computes per-mile tire expense from tire set cost, expected life, retread cycles, and position-specific wear factors.
Computes expected battery replacement timing from age, climate factor, voltage trend inputs, and preventive-maintenance thresholds.
Computes trailer turn time from drop, unload, reload, and release milestones using configurable inclusion rules for yard dwell.
Computes container per diem charges from free-time clocks, calendar type, terminal rules, and daily tiered rates.
Computes demurrage from terminal dwell beyond free time, storage calendars, merchant-haulage rules, and escalating rate schedules.
Computes chassis split charges from terminal and yard locations, extra dray miles, dual transaction rules, and contractual fees.
Computes drayage turn time from in-gate, out-gate, and terminal transaction milestones with split-move handling rules.
Computes congestion surcharges from terminal congestion tier, transaction type, appointment delays, and effective-date business rules.
Computes brokerage-related charges from border crossing type, entry count, commodity complexity, and tariff or pass-through rules.
